newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says repulses Eritrean attack in northeast.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says repulses Eritrean attack in northeast.

text.p: A Sudanese army spokesman said on Wednesday government troops had repulsed attacks by Eritrean forces in the northeast near the border with Eritrea.

A government newspaper also said on Wednesday the country's armed forces had recaptured areas in central Sudan which had been under rebel control for at least 10 years and released hundreds of people trapped there.

Khartoum's Islamist government has accused Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of fighting alongside northern and southern rebels to overthrow President Omar Hassan al-Bashir. All three countries deny the charge.
The rebel coalition under the command of Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) leader John Garang has said it is behind the fighting in Sudan's northeast and southern areas.

"Eritrean forces at dawn today undertook fresh attacks on the areas of Togan, Gadamait and Kadamet," said army spokesman Lieutenant General Mohammad al-Sanousi Ahmad in a statement broadcast on the official Omdurman radio.
Ahmad said the attack started with mortar shelling.
"Then they attacked Togan with forces of about an infantry battalion supported by four tanks and four armoured personnel carriers," he said.
"But thanks to God, the brave armed forces stationed in these areas repulsed the attack and expelled the attackers who fled leaving behind their dead and equipment," he added.
Ahmad did not give casualty figures for either side.

The government-owned Sudan al-Hadith newspaper said on Wednesday: "The People's Defence Forces undertook a successful campaign at the mountains around Dilling (in Southern Kordofan state), and on the border of Rashad and Kadguli provinces."
The daily named areas "cleared from the rebels" as Abyad town, which lies some 150 km (94 miles) away from Dilling, al-Mur, Jebel Makar, Sharaf and Shambarna.

The paper said the army had also taken control for the first time in 13 years the road linking Talodi town in the southeast with Malakal, one of the main towns in the south. It said the route between Talodi and Kadguli in the east was in state hands.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north.
SPLA leader Garang offered in a statement issued in Nairobi on Wednesday to swap 300 captured government soldiers for five rebels seized by a force allied with Khartoum in south Sudan late last year.
